Privacy Policy

Information you share

The enquiry form asks for your name, email, phone number, support needs and consent to be contacted. You may also share your company, preferred start date and time zone. We use Web3Forms to forward enquiries to our business support inbox. When you contact us directly, we receive the information and follow-up messages you share.

Website visits and cookies

The hosting service may receive technical information such as your IP address, browser type and the pages you request. It may use those details to deliver the website, troubleshoot problems and protect the service. AssistLane Global does not currently add analytics or advertising cookies to this website.

How we use information

We use the details you share to answer questions, understand the work you need and discuss a possible engagement. If you become a client, we use relevant information to manage and deliver the agreed services. We may also keep records to document our communications and meet applicable legal obligations.

Who can access information

The people who handle your enquiry or engagement may access the information they need for that work. Providers that host the site or support our business communications may process information to provide their services. We may also disclose information when the law requires it.

Providers may process information in the countries where they operate. Where rules on international transfers apply, we use the safeguards those rules require.

How long we keep information

We keep enquiry correspondence for as long as we need it to respond and follow up. If an enquiry leads to client work, we keep the records needed to provide and document the agreed services. Contractual or legal recordkeeping requirements may affect how long we keep either type of record.

Information we handle for clients

During client work, we follow the agreed instructions and access permissions for the records a client makes available. If your request concerns information a client controls, contact that organisation.

At handover, we agree with the client which working copies to return or remove and which records they need to keep. We also agree who checks that access to the accounts and shared files used for the work has been removed. Read about Trust and Security for more on access and handovers.

Your privacy rights

Depending on applicable law, you may have the right to request access to your information, ask us to correct or delete it, or object to or restrict certain uses. Where we rely on consent, you may withdraw it. You may also have the right to raise a concern with the relevant data protection authority. We may ask for enough information to confirm your identity and locate your records.

Privacy contact and updates

Send privacy questions or requests to AssistLane Global using the email below. When emailing, use “Privacy request” as the subject and tell us what you’d like us to do. Include the email address you used for your enquiry if you have one.

Privacy email support@assistlaneglobal.com

We post updates to this policy on this page.

Planning your support

Open the topics that matter to your team. These details explain how to prepare the work, review results and handle changes.

Understanding your information

What to include in a first enquiry

A first enquiry only needs enough information for us to understand the kind of support you want and how to reply. A business name, a contact email and a general description of the task are usually more useful than a full set of customer records. You can describe the number of requests, the systems involved and the result you need without naming every person in those records. If an example contains private information, replace the names and identifying details before sharing it. Contact us first if you are unsure whether a document is necessary.

Optional contact and planning details

The website form identifies the information needed to send an enquiry. A phone number is optional. You may also choose to provide your company, a preferred start date and a time zone. Those details help explain your working arrangements, but leaving an optional field empty should not stop you from asking a question. If you give us a contact number, explain whether you prefer a call or an email response. Please check that the email address belongs to you or that you are authorised to use it for the enquiry.

Information sent through an online form

When an online enquiry form is available, the information you submit is processed through Web3Forms so it can reach the business enquiry inbox. The provider may also process technical information to operate its service and detect abuse. Its own privacy policy explains its processing and retention arrangements. You can read that policy at Web3Forms privacy information. The form is for an initial conversation about support. Please do not use it to send passwords, payment credentials, identity documents or confidential client files. You can instead ask us which approved channel should be used for a particular document.

Following up on an existing conversation

A reply may contain the earlier message, attachments you choose to include and the contact details of people copied into the conversation. Think about who needs to receive the reply before adding another address. A short reference to the previous enquiry can help us locate the discussion without sending the same material again. If you have used more than one email address, tell us which address relates to the request. Please avoid forwarding an entire internal conversation when a short description of the relevant question will give us enough context to help.

Separating an enquiry from client work

An initial enquiry does not by itself provide access to your business systems or permission to work with other people’s records. Before client work begins, the parties need to agree the task, the authorised systems and the people who can approve access. Client instructions and contractual arrangements may describe responsibilities more specifically than this website notice. If you are asking about information held by one of our clients, that client may need to decide how the request should be handled. We should not change a client-controlled record simply because a third party has requested it.

Keeping shared examples proportionate

The amount of information needed depends on the task being discussed. A calendar example may only need the date, duration and type of meeting. An order-support example may only need a fictional reference and a description of the issue. Remove account credentials and unnecessary personal details before you share a sample. If a task later requires access to identifiable records, agree that access separately with the responsible owner. This approach helps the first conversation stay focused on what the assistant needs to do and prevents an example from becoming an unnecessary copy of a larger business record.

Account access and working copies

Where client work involves an account, the account owner should approve the role and the actions allowed under it. A link to an approved record can sometimes provide enough context without copying the entire file into an email. The appropriate storage location, access permissions and arrangements for working copies should form part of the agreed setup. If an instruction changes, the people responsible for the work need to know which version now applies. Questions about a client’s original account, access logs or records may need to be answered by the organisation that controls that system.

Technical information and linked websites

Your browser must exchange technical information with the services that deliver a website. That exchange can include an IP address, the requested page and information about the browser making the request. Technical records may help providers identify failed requests or protect the service from abuse. A link to another website takes you to a service with its own information practices. Read the relevant notice before entering information there. This website notice describes AssistLane Global’s enquiries and agreed work; it does not replace the separate notices published by email, hosting or other service providers.

Understanding how long a record is needed

Different records can serve different purposes. A short question about availability may need a different follow-up from an active client engagement with ongoing instructions. Information may also remain in an email conversation or another approved system used for that relationship. We have not published one fixed retention period for every type of record. When you ask about a particular record, identify the conversation or engagement so the relevant purpose and any applicable obligations can be considered. A deletion request may need to distinguish unnecessary working copies from records that still have to be retained for a legitimate reason.

Making a clear privacy request

Send your request to support@assistlaneglobal.com with Privacy request in the subject. Describe the information or conversation you mean and what you would like us to do. For example, you might explain that an enquiry contains an old contact number or that you want to understand what information was received through a particular message. Include a useful date or reference where you have one. Please do not send identity documents unless an appropriate verification route has been agreed. We may need to clarify the request or confirm that it concerns information you are entitled to ask about.
